models.notes: Quantization-aware training, not a post-hoc quantization: the damage is trained around rather than measured after. Estimated memory is 7089 MiB of weights, about 832 MiB of KV cache at 8192 tokens (Gemma 3 interleaves five 1024-token local layers per global one, so long contexts cost far less than the layer count suggests), and roughly 1.3 GiB of compute buffer and runtime overhead. Weights are the ungated unsloth mirror because google/gemma-3-12b-it-qat-q4_0-gguf is gated 'manual' on Hugging Face and a downloader with no account cannot fetch it. Gemma is Google's open-weight family, run locally under the user's control.

The catalogue's best rewriter, above Qwen3.8 27B (D853): on the prompt bench of October it passed 95.9 % of attempts against Qwen3.8's 93.1 %, the judge found the meaning changed in 7–8 % of paraphrases against 20 %, at twice the speed — and on the bench of 2026-11-19 it changed the meaning least of the five rewriters measured (7 %), and rewrote deepest. So it is every machine's default wherever it has room (D854). Pinned to commit f18012b8, the last whose file is the one the local engine was measured on (E2-4: all 48 layers offloaded, 57 tokens a second); the repository's later re-upload carries an updated chat template that has not been checked against the renderer. Gemma 4's chat format is rendered by wipemark_llama::chat with thinking off (D181), because llama.cpp's built-in list does not know it. Memory: 6405 MiB of weights, about 832 MiB of context cache at 8192 tokens (Gemma 4 keeps Gemma 3's sliding 1024-token layers, so the cache is taken as Gemma 3 12B's) and about 1.3 GiB of compute buffer and overhead, rounded up to 8704 MiB. The header-based estimate over-states this model's cache several times over (its sliding layers are counted as full), which is why the figure is set here rather than computed; the resident memory measured after a load (D55) is the number to check it against. Apache 2.0, Google's licence for Gemma 4 (the model card and its licence page); the file's header still says gemma (D851).

The default where only about 3 GB is free for a model — an 8 GB Mac, an 8 GB card, 6 GB of RAM with no card measured (D854) — in Qwen3 4B's place. It loads and rewrites at the pin, b10731 (D855). Asked in English it answers a Russian text in English (E2-4); the pipeline asks for a Russian or German document in that language, and so does its live gate. Apache 2.0, Google's licence for Gemma 4 (the model card and its licence page); the file's header says gemma. Memory, as llama.cpp at the pin sizes it at 8192 tokens: 2700 MiB of weights (the file's 2499 and a second copy of the token embeddings for the output head), 60 MiB of context cache at F16 (32 MiB at the engine's Q8_0: 15 of its 35 layers keep one, 3 full-attention layers of one 512-wide head and 12 sliding 512-token ones) and 158 MiB of compute buffers; and about 0.9 GiB for the GPU runtime and the process, 3840 MiB in all. Of the weights, 1476 MiB (the per-layer and token embeddings) stay in host memory and are read a row at a time. On a 16 GB card (Vulkan, every layer, 4096 tokens) the live gate's process held 1793 MiB of the card, about 430 MiB above its buffers.

Stable since D852, once the bench had measured it against the stable entries on the whole corpus (2026-11-19, judged by Gemma 4 12B): the meaning changed in 13 % of paraphrases at moderate strength, tied with Gemma 4 E4B's 12 %; it passed 98.3 % of attempts, the most of the five measured, kept every markdown item, and had the best Russian of the small ones (9 % changed, against E4B's 18 %) — but rewrote less deeply (25 % of word pairs carried over, against 17 %) and worse in German (21 % against 15 %). Tied with E4B and 0.8 GB larger, it comes after it and is no machine's default (D854): chosen by the person, for Russian above all. NVIDIA's post-training of Gemma 4 E4B: 8B parameters, 4B effective (per-layer embeddings). unsloth's UD-Q4_K_XL, pinned at b738967d, rather than NVIDIA's own Q4_K_M (6.18 GB, its per-layer and token embeddings at Q8_0, no licence in its header): ungated, and its header names openmdw-1.1. It loads at the engine's pin: llama.cpp b10731 creates the K and V projections of its 18 shared-cache layers, which NVIDIA's conversion keeps and Gemma 4 E4B's files do not, as optional tensors. Its chat template is NVIDIA's updated Gemma 4 one, thinking off by default, rendered by wipemark_llama::chat with the bare opener; <turn|> ends a turn by its text, as the file names no end-of-turn token. Trained languages: en, fr, de, zh, ja, pt, vi, it, es, ko, hi, ar. Asked in English it answers German and Russian text in English; the pipeline asks for a German or Russian document in that language, and on the bench (paraphrase, moderate, every third item, an M3 Pro, Metal) 195 of 196 attempts passed, the one refusal a Russian answer in another language, against Qwen3 4B's 166 on the same grid that day. A document in a language with no shipped templates is asked in English and may come back translated, which the language check refuses. Memory: 4826 MiB of weights, about 168 MiB of KV cache at 8192 tokens (24 of its 42 layers keep one: 4 full-attention layers of two 512-wide heads, 20 sliding 512-token ones) and about 1.6 GiB of compute buffer and overhead, rounded up to 6656 MiB; on Metal at 4096 tokens the test process peaked at 4.6 GB, the per-layer embeddings read a row at a time. Not its DFlash drafter: NVIDIA's has no selector (DFlash 1, which the engine refuses, D481) and asks for llama.cpp b11808.

4.0B parameters, 3.6B of them outside the embeddings. The 2507 Instruct build and not the hybrid Qwen3-4B on purpose: the hybrid reasons before it answers, and the measurement recorded in dev/sdd/layer-b-rewrite-reference.md is 9894 completion tokens against 12 for the same rewrite. A rewriter that thinks out loud is paying for tokens nobody reads. Estimated memory is 2429 MiB of weights, 1152 MiB of KV cache at 8192 tokens, and about 1 GiB of compute buffer and overhead. No machine's default since D854: on the bench of 2026-11-19 it was the worst of the five rewriters on every quality measure — the meaning changed in 40 % of paraphrases (German 63 %), planted instructions obeyed 30 % of the time — and Gemma 4 E2B, as small, changed it in 22 %. It stays in the catalogue for those who have it.

27B parameters at unsloth's dynamic IQ3_S, about 3.6 bits a weight. A hybrid model whose chat template has a thinking switch: wipemark_llama::chat renders it with thinking off (D182), because llama.cpp's built-in ChatML opener is the template's thinking-on. Memory: 11 483 MiB of weights, and the rest of 14 GiB for the context cache at 8192 tokens, the compute buffer and the process around them. Measured in E2-4 on a 16 GB card: 62 of its 65 layers fitted beside another process, at 10.9 tokens a second; the application asks llama.cpp for every layer on the GPU, so a card that cannot hold the whole model refuses the load (LoadFailed) rather than splitting it. Below Gemma 4 12B since D853: the October bench measured it behind on every quality measure and at half the speed, so it is chosen by the person and no machine's default.

Not a model that writes: a DFlash2 block-diffusion draft trained for Qwen3.8 27B, which proposes up to seven tokens a step for that model to verify in one decode (E2-dflash2, D484). With greedy decoding the text is the model's own; with sampling every token is still the model's draw. Q4_K_M because the card measures it at least as well as Q8_0 (acceptance length 5.39 against 5.13, eight GSM8K prompts) and it is the smallest; the mirror of incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-GGUF, pinned at 2d9571f8, its sha256 and size read off Hugging Face's tree API and its resolve endpoint. Memory, from the two models' config.json: 1091 MiB of weights; 160 MiB of KV cache at 8192 tokens (five layers of eight 128-wide KV heads, F16 — four of five are sliding 2048-token layers, so less in practice); 1047 MiB for the seven extra snapshots of Qwen3.8's recurrent state the model keeps to roll back a rejected block (48 Gated DeltaNet layers of about 3.1 MiB each); 200 MiB for the five layer inputs the draft reads (5 x 5120 x 2048 floats); and about 300 MiB of compute buffer — 2798, rounded up to 2816, on top of the model's own figure.
